Select LHWR Bandwidth

Source: R/bandwidth.R
bw.lhwr.Rd

Select the kernel bandwidth used by LHWR local regressions. Candidate Gaussian bandwidths are scored by corrected Akaike information criterion (AICc) or leave-one-out squared-error cross-validation (CV). Binomial bandwidths are scored by leave-one-out Bernoulli log loss. The selected bandwidth is the candidate with the smallest score.

Usage

bw.lhwr(
  formula,
  data,
  Z,
  approach = c("AICc", "CV"),
  kernel = hgwr_kernel_names(),
  adaptive = TRUE,
  bandwidth_type = c("knn", "volume"),
  search = NULL,
  geometry = c("lorentz", "tangent"),
  bw_grid = NULL,
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  tol = 1e-04,
  max_iter = 200L,
  pilot_k = NULL,
  tangent_ref = NULL,
  dMat = NULL,
  engine = c("dense", "knn"),
  n_threads = 1L,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  control = stats::glm.control(maxit = 100L)
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula of the form response ~ predictors.

data

Data frame containing the response and predictor variables used in formula.

Z

Numeric n x 3 matrix of Lorentz hyperboloid coordinates. Row i gives the location of observation i and must satisfy <z_i,z_i>_L = -1 with positive time coordinate.

approach

Bandwidth selection criterion. "AICc" minimizes the corrected Akaike information criterion computed from the local fitted values and hat-matrix trace. "CV" minimizes the leave-one-out prediction error.

kernel

Kernel used to convert distances into local weights. Available choices are "bisquare", "gaussian", "exponential", "tricube", and "boxcar".

adaptive

Logical. If TRUE, scalar bandwidths are interpreted as neighbor counts and converted to location-specific radii. If FALSE, scalar bandwidths are interpreted as fixed radii, or fixed hyperbolic volumes when bandwidth_type = "volume".

bandwidth_type

Bandwidth scale. "knn" uses the radius to the requested nearest neighbor. "volume" uses a hyperbolic ball-volume interpretation and is available only for geometry = "lorentz".

search

Bandwidth search method. "golden" uses golden-section optimization over an automatically chosen interval. "grid" evaluates the supplied candidate values in bw_grid. If omitted, "golden" is used when bw_grid is NULL, and "grid" is used when bw_grid is supplied.

geometry

Distance geometry used to build kernel weights. "lorentz" uses intrinsic hyperbolic distances on the Lorentz hyperboloid. "tangent" maps locations to one tangent plane by the Lorentz logarithmic map and uses the positive-definite Lorentz metric induced on that tangent plane. Equivalently, these distances can be represented as Euclidean distances in a Lorentz-orthonormal tangent basis.

bw_grid

Optional numeric vector of candidate bandwidths for search = "grid". In adaptive fits these are neighbor counts; in fixed fits these are radii unless bandwidth_type = "volume".

lower

Optional lower search bound for search = "golden".

upper

Optional upper search bound for search = "golden".

tol

Golden-section stopping tolerance.

max_iter

Maximum number of golden-section iterations.

pilot_k

Pilot neighbor count used to estimate local point density for adaptive volume bandwidths. Ignored unless adaptive = TRUE and bandwidth_type = "volume".

tangent_ref

Optional reference point for geometry = "tangent". If omitted, the normalized extrinsic Lorentz mean is used.

dMat

Optional precomputed n x n distance matrix. If supplied, it is used directly and geometry is used only for labeling and validation of related arguments.

engine

Computational engine. "dense" builds or uses a full distance matrix. "knn" uses exact Lorentz nearest-neighbor lists and avoids storing the full distance matrix; it is available for adaptive Lorentz kNN fits with compact kernels.

n_threads

Number of OpenMP threads used by engine = "knn" when OpenMP is available. The default 1 preserves serial execution.

family

Response family. Gaussian LHWR supports "AICc" and "CV"; binomial LHWR supports "CV" and uses leave-one-out Bernoulli log loss. When family = "binomial" and approach is omitted, "CV" is selected.

control

Iteration controls for binomial LHWR, created by stats::glm.control(). Ignored for Gaussian bandwidth selection.

Value

An object of class "bw.lhwr", a list containing the selected bandwidth (bw), selection criterion (approach), kernel, geometry, search method, selected score, AICc/CV fields when applicable, hat-matrix trace (trS), residual sum of squares (RSS), the evaluated selection.table, and the original function call.

Details

AICc and CV are selection criteria; post-fit AIC and BIC are not additional choices for approach. Gaussian CV is a sum of squared leave-one-out errors, using the supplied representation and candidate radii. It does not relearn the representation or reselect bandwidth within an outer validation loop. AICc is infinite when its denominator n - tr(S) - 2 is nonpositive.

The adaptive neighbour rank is not a guarantee of exactly that many positive kernel weights. Compact kernels have zero boundary weight; ties and coincident locations matter. Inspect local positive-weight counts and effective support. Grid search identifies the minimum among evaluated candidates; review boundary selections before making a scientifically justified change to the search. See vignette("lhwr-diagnostics-and-tuning", package = "LHWL") for the criterion formulas, kernel curves, volume rules and engine compatibility.

Examples

set.seed(20260615)
n <- 120
H <- simulate_H2(n, r_max = 5, uniform_area = TRUE)
Z <- H$Z
D <- hyperbolic_distance_matrix(Z, check = FALSE)

true_k <- 25
h <- apply(D, 1, function(d) sort(d[d > 0])[true_k])
centers <- round(seq(10, n - 10, length.out = 5))
Phi <- sapply(centers, function(j) {
  hgwr_kernel(D[, j], h[j], kernel = "bisquare")
})

beta0 <- 0.4 + 2 * (1.45 * Phi[, 1] - 1.25 * Phi[, 4])
beta1 <- 1.0 + 2 * (1.65 * Phi[, 2] - 1.20 * Phi[, 5])
beta2 <- -0.8 + 2 * (1.55 * Phi[, 3] - 1.10 * Phi[, 4])

x1 <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
x2 <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
eta <- beta0 + beta1 * x1 + beta2 * x2
y <- eta + rnorm(n, sd = sqrt(var(eta) / 8))
dat <- data.frame(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2)

bw <- bw.lhwr(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = Z,
  approach = "CV",
  kernel = "bisquare",
  adaptive = TRUE,
  geometry = "lorentz",
  bw_grid = seq(10, 80, by = 5)
)
bw
head(bw$selection.table)
